 Economic Indicators Wholesale prices are up 6.5% from a year ago, the biggest annual rise since November 2022
 Producer prices rose 0.3% in October from September, below the 0.4% economists expected, as truck freight costs climbed
 By Cris Tolomia · 2 min read · Updated November 13, 2026 Add QZ to Google NurPhoto / Getty Images
 The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October from September on a seasonally adjusted basis. On an unadjusted basis, the producer price index for final demand climbed 6.5% over the year through October, its biggest annual increase since a 7.4% gain in November 2022.
 The monthly gain followed a 1.4% increase in September and a 0.4% increase in August. The 0.3% rise in October was below the 0.4% Dow Jones consensus forecast, according to CNBC .
 Final demand goods prices rose 0.5% in October after a 2.5% rise in September. Food prices increased 1.3%, while energy prices edged down 0.1%. Basic organic chemicals advanced 3.9%, and diesel fuel prices fell 7.9%. For the 12 months ended in October, goods prices rose 10.2%, the largest annual gain since a 10.5% rise in October 2022.
 Final demand services prices moved up 0.2%, the fifth consecutive monthly advance. Prices for transportation and warehousing services rose 2.0%. Over 80% of the October increase in services is attributable to truck transportation of freight, which climbed 3.9%. Margins for final demand trade services decreased 0.2%.
 The index for final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% in October, the same as in September. That measure advanced 4.9% from a year earlier.
 Prices further back in the supply chain also showed large annual gains. Processed goods for intermediate demand rose 14.6% for the 12 months ended in October, the largest 12-month rise since a 17.2% increase in July 2022. Prices for services for intermediate demand rose 6.8%, the largest 12-month advance since a 6.9% gain in November 2022.
 Unprocessed goods for intermediate demand fell 3.1% in October, the largest decline since a 6.6% drop in June. Crude petroleum prices decreased 10.3%. Unprocessed goods were still up 16.9% from a year earlier.
 The Iran war, along with the energy supply disruption it set off, has lifted costs at the gas and diesel pump over the past several months, according to CNN .
 Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said inflation has been broad-based. "If you look at how broad-based the inflation is, it's not just that we're above the target and have been for some time. It's that in categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you're still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way," Goolsbee told CNBC.
 The bureau is scheduled to publish the November producer price index on Tuesday, Dec. 15, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
